text_blocks.snippet: Hughes disease, also known as Antiphospholipid Syndrome (APS), is an autoimmune disorder where the body's immune system mistakenly attacks healthy cells, specifically phospholipids in the blood. This leads to an increased risk of blood clots forming in both arteries and veins, potentially causing serious complications like stroke, heart attack, and miscarriage.
snippet_highlighted_words: an autoimmune disorder where the body's immune system mistakenly attacks healthy cells, specifically phospholipids in the blood

list.title: Autoimmune Nature:
list.snippet: APS is an autoimmune disease, meaning the body's immune system, which normally fights off infections, mistakenly attacks the body's own tissues.

list.title: Antibodies:
list.snippet: In APS, the immune system produces antibodies called antiphospholipid antibodies that target phospholipids, which are components of cell membranes.

list.title: Blood Clotting:
list.snippet: These antibodies can cause blood clots (thrombosis) to form in both arteries and veins, potentially leading to a range of health issues.

list.title: Pregnancy Complications:
list.snippet: APS can also cause complications during pregnancy, including miscarriage, stillbirth, and premature birth.
